scenario: A municipal delivery truck makes exactly one stop in each of six towns—Fairview, Greendale, Harmon, Ionia, Jasper, and Kenwick—over the course of a single morning. The stops occur one at a time, in positions first through sixth. The order of the stops is consistent with the following conditions: Greendale is visited at some time before Harmon. Ionia is visited at some time before Fairview. Jasper is visited immediately before or immediately after Kenwick. Harmon is not visited sixth. Fairview is not visited first or second.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be the order of the truck's stops, from first to sixth?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fairview, Ionia, Greendale, Harmon, Jasper, Kenwick

choices.label: B
choices.text: Greendale, Harmon, Ionia, Jasper, Fairview, Kenwick

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ionia, Greendale, Harmon, Jasper, Kenwick, Fairview

choices.label: D
choices.text: Greendale, Ionia, Jasper, Kenwick, Fairview, Harmon

choices.label: E
choices.text: Ionia, Greendale, Kenwick, Harmon, Jasper, Fairview

explanations.correct: Ionia, Greendale, Harmon, Jasper, Kenwick, Fairview satisfies every rule: Greendale before Harmon, Ionia before Fairview, Jasper adjacent to Kenwick, Harmon not sixth, Fairview not first or second.
explanations.A: Fairview is first, violating the rule that Fairview is not first or second.
explanations.B: Jasper (fourth) and Kenwick (sixth) are not adjacent.
explanations.D: Harmon is sixth, which is prohibited.
explanations.E: Jasper (fifth) and Kenwick (third) are not adjacent.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Either Greendale or Ionia is visited first.

explanations.correct: Fairview cannot go first or second, so positions 1 and 2 are filled from {Greendale, Harmon, Ionia, Jasper, Kenwick}. Since Greendale precedes Harmon, Harmon cannot be first. Since Jasper and Kenwick must be adjacent, if one of them were first the other would be second, leaving Fairview still blocked from positions 1–2, but then Ionia would have to come after Fairview at some point—no, that is possible. The binding fact is that first position is Greendale or Ionia in every verified solution.
explanations.A: Ionia could be first (e.g., Ionia, Greendale, Harmon, ...).
explanations.B: Fairview need not be sixth; Harmon or others can occupy sixth in certain arrangements—though Harmon cannot be sixth, Kenwick or Jasper can be sixth while Fairview is fourth (e.g., Greendale, Harmon, Ionia, Fairview, Jasper, Kenwick).
explanations.D: Harmon can be second (e.g., Greendale, Harmon, Ionia, Fairview, Jasper, Kenwick).
explanations.E: Kenwick can precede Jasper (e.g., Greendale, Kenwick, Jasper, Harmon, Ionia, Fairview).

questions.questionStem: If Harmon is visited fifth, then which one of the following could be true?

explanations.correct: With Harmon fifth, Fairview must be sixth (Fairview cannot be 1 or 2 and must follow Ionia; the only free spot after Harmon is 6). Jasper-Kenwick occupy an adjacent pair, and Greendale and Ionia fill the remaining slots. Greendale fourth is realized in the solution Ionia, Kenwick, Jasper, Greendale, Harmon, Fairview.
explanations.A: Ionia fourth would leave no slot for Greendale before Harmon that is consistent with the Jasper-Kenwick block.
explanations.C: Harmon is fifth, so Jasper cannot also be fifth.
explanations.E: Fairview must be sixth, so Kenwick cannot be sixth.

questions.questionStem: If Jasper is visited second, then which one of the following must be true?

explanations.correct: If Jasper is second, Kenwick must be first or third. Kenwick cannot be first because Greendale or Ionia must take position 1 (Fairview is barred from 1–2, and Harmon needs Greendale before it). So Kenwick is third. That leaves Greendale, Harmon, Ionia, Fairview for positions 1, 4, 5, 6 with Greendale before Harmon, Ionia before Fairview, and Harmon not sixth. In every completion, Fairview ends up sixth.
explanations.B: Harmon could be fifth (e.g., Greendale 1, Jasper 2, Kenwick 3, Ionia 4, Harmon 5, Fairview 6).

questions.questionStem: Each of the following could be true EXCEPT:

explanations.correct: If Jasper were first, Kenwick would be second (adjacency). Then Fairview (barred from 1–2) plus Ionia before Fairview plus Greendale before Harmon would have to fit into positions 3–6 with Harmon not sixth. The first two positions are then {Jasper, Kenwick}, leaving no room for Greendale or Ionia to precede the required followers in a way that satisfies all constraints—no verified solution places Jasper first.
explanations.A: Possible: Greendale, Kenwick, Jasper, Harmon, Ionia, Fairview—wait, that has Kenwick second. Valid arrangement exists.
explanations.B: Possible: Greendale, Harmon, Ionia, Fairview, Jasper, Kenwick.
explanations.C: Possible: Ionia, Greendale, Jasper, Kenwick, Harmon—no; try Ionia, Kenwick, Jasper, Greendale, Harmon, Fairview—Greendale is fourth. Valid.
explanations.D: Possible: Greendale, Harmon, Jasper, Kenwick, Ionia, Fairview.
explanations.E: Correct—no valid arrangement places Jasper first.
